environment_concept: A lane of tall reeds that rustle and whisper in the wind, leading to a small lit stone shelter. The whisper is only the sound of reeds; no whisperer, jinn or person is shown.

unique_world.visual_theme: A village on a clear morning with a winding lane past an orchard, a pond and a market to Grandmother's house

primary_mechanic.text: Carry a sealed letter to Grandmother; at three places a bad thought comes (skip the errand, read the letter, keep the sweets), shown only as a grey mist. Seeking refuge in the Lord of people clears it; listening thickens the mist; obeying is refused; delivering before every mist is cleared is refused (114:1-5). No whisperer or jinn is shown.

unique_world.narrative_structure: A reading at the top of the lane, the errand, then a reading by the market
environment_behaviour: the mist grows when listened to and disappears when turned from
unique_world.learning_objective: Seek refuge in the Lord of people from the whisperer who withdraws (114:1-4)

story_library.source: Owner's 'Quran Adventure — Children's Story Library' (2026-11-04), first-draft narration for ages about 7-12
story_library.title: The Safe Place
story_library.children_narration: Sometimes unhelpful thoughts or suggestions can lead us toward wrong choices. Surah An-Nas teaches us to seek refuge in Allah, the Lord, King, and God of humanity, from evil whispering. We can ask Allah for help and choose what is good.

world_idea.title: The Sanctuary of Peace
world_idea.description: Explore a comforting, carefully designed environment about making good choices. Complete simple activities distinguishing helpful suggestions from harmful ones. Do not depict Allah, jinn, or unseen whisperers. ## Final content checklist Surah coverage in this response 104 / 104 All remaining surahs, 11 through 114, now have introductory English narration, Quran references, and a proposed personalized 3D world. Important distinction: This completes the introductory content outline for the remaining 104 surahs, not the full set of stories contained in them. For example, Surah Hud needs separate complete narratives for Nuh, Hud, Salih, Ibrahim, Lut, Shu'ayb, and Musa. Other long surahs also require multiple chapters and coverage of teachings not included in these short summaries. The next content-development stage should expand each entry into full narration scripts, playable scenes, child actions, learning objectives, and exact ayah-to-scene mappings. Every script will also need review against reliable tafsir by a qualified Quran scholar before public release. For source verification and future expansion, use  for the full surahs, translations, and tafsir access, alongside a verified Quran-text database.  [image](https://www.google.com/s2/favicons?domain=https://islamtics.com\&sz=32) Islamtics+2 My strongest recommendation is to keep each surah's world distinct while linking stories shared between multiple surahs. That will let children visit all 114 worlds without encountering the same adventure repeatedly under different names.
